Feature: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
Comment: The pronominal system is nominative-accusative, but the first, second and third person singular free pronouns and the first and third person singular bound pronouns follow the ergative-absolutive pattern as well as the nominative-accusative.
curated_comment: CORRECTED 1 -> 0. The singular free pronouns are NOT cleanly ergative-absolutive. The regular paradigm (Oates 1988:89-90, Table 4.1) is nominative-accusative: bare NOM serves S and A (1sg ngathu), a distinct ACC serves P (1sg nga-nha). Ergative -ngku then OPTIONALLY marks A (ex.4.85 ngathu-ngku '1sg.ERG'). Combining these, A=ERG(-ngku), S=bare NOM, P=ACC(-nha) are three distinct forms; Oates 1988:100 (Table 4.2) explicitly frames this as an 'ergative-accusative' system overlapping with nominative-accusative. Since S != P (S bare, P accusative), there is no ergative ALIGNMENT (which requires S=P): the pattern is tripartite (or nom-acc), not ergative. Per the tripartite rule (tripartite S/A/P -> 0), coding 0.

A, S and P are marked by three different forms = tripartite, not ergative-absolutive. Per the tripartite rule, coding 0.

curated_comment: CORRECTED 1 -> 0. 3sg free pronoun has NO ergative form: Oates 1988:100 (Table 4.2) lists 3sg A only as nhumpu with no -ngku variant, and no nhumpu-ngku is attested. The 3sg system is nominative-accusative: A=S=nhumpu (ex.4.98-4.100) vs distinct ACC pu-nha (Table 4.1; ex.4.101 nhumpu in O function is the syncretised NOM). With A=S, there is no ergative alignment on 3sg pronouns. Coding 0.
